item.title: Euronews: Darth Vader's lightsaber breaks Star Wars auction record by selling for nearly €4.5 million
item.description: Auctioneers estimated the on screen prop would sell for over $1m, but the lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the famous “I am your father” scene ended up selling for nearly $5m.

item.title: Euronews: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave one dead in Odesa
item.description: Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine killed at least one person in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters battled the flames.

item.title: Euronews: ExxonMobil sues EU over rules forcing oil giants to invest in carbon storage
item.description: US oil giant ExxonMobil is challenging EU rules requiring fossil fuel producers to help fund carbon storage infrastructure, in a legal battle that could undermine Brussels’ efforts to make the industry pay for the energy transition.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: L’objectif de 1,5° de réchauffement est mort, mais personne ne veut l’enterrer
item.description: Les dirigeants présents à la COP31 s'attachent à cet objectif emblématique, même après que l'ONU et de nombreux scientifiques ont déclaré qu'il était impossible à atteindre.

item.title: Euronews: Why the UK wants to jail undersea cable saboteurs and why tougher punishment may not be enough
item.description: The United Kingdom is seeking tougher penalties for damaging critical underwater infrastructure, but industry insiders warn that stronger rules alone cannot prevent widespread disruption.

item.title: Euronews: Microsoft outage explained: what went wrong and is your data at risk?
item.description: Governments, doctor surgeries and even rival AI firms have been caught up, and the episode is sharpening questions about Europe's reliance on a handful of US tech giants.

item.title: Euronews: Dementia risk increases with number of cigarettes smoked per day
item.description: Researchers found that dementia risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day, rising by 16% for those who smoke 10 a day and by 34% for those who smoke 20, compared with people who have never smoked.

item.title: Euronews: IRGC says it destroyed US radar in Bahrain after attack on southern Iran
item.description: Despite rising military tensions, diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are continuing. Tehran has made any resumption of formal negotiations with Washington conditional on its demands being met.

item.title: Euronews: José Pinhal's rediscovered songs sell out Porto and Lisbon Coliseums
item.description: A tribute band to an artist who was only known in an ultra-restricted circle while alive sent the Coliseu dos Recreios wild at its farewell concert. Understanding the José Pinhal phenomenon means grasping our century's drive to reclaim nuggets from the past.

item.title: Euronews: Swedish pop sensation Robyn brands Eurovision ‘embarrassing’
item.description: Swedish pop star Robyn, whose hits include 'With Every Heartbeat' and 'Dancing On My Own', shared her verdict on Eurovision during an appearance on Amy Poehler's podcast. She suggested Eurovision's appeal had diminished for her since ABBA’s involvement, and that it was "embarrassing".

item.title: Euronews: What is next for Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang resigns?
item.description: The AI chip giant has no leader in waiting, may lose its voice in Washington, and has big bets in Europe that its founder championed in person.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Spain’s Sánchez laments potential for ‘planetary annihilation’
item.description: The Spanish leader urges major reform of the United Nations and warns that the EU's embrace of “war preparedness” is feeding “a dangerous militaristic mindset.”

item.title: Euronews: Portugal: Humanoid robots take centre stage at Web Summit 2026
item.description: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs stole the show at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal's economy over the past decade, according to a study.

item.title: Euronews: Outlook outage: how to keep working and which email alternatives you can use
item.description: After Microsoft 365 services went down on 12 November, affecting millions of users worldwide, here is how you can keep using Outlook while the issue is fixed.

item.title: Euronews: Flying Blue flies high: These are the best airline rewards programmes in Europe
item.description: Air France-KLM's Flying Blue was crowned the best frequent flyer scheme globally thanks to how easy it is to earn and spend miles. The British Airways Club and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club also ranked high.

item.title: Euronews: 'The market will look for alternatives,' on Huang resignation says Andrea Renda, Digital Economy expert
item.description: Nvidia is at the centre of the global artificial intelligence revolution. But the American chip giant is now facing an extraordinary crisis, following the shock resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of an espionage scandal.

item.title: Euronews: 'The structure of the European economy needs to change more quickly,' says IMF Europe chief Mateusz Szczurek
item.description: Europe's economy is facing a dangerous combination of challenges: sluggish growth, mounting public debt and rising borrowing costs. As sovereign bond yields put pressure on government finances, Europe's ability to invest in its future is increasingly in question.

item.title: Euronews: European shares fall as Nvidia CEO’s exit raises doubts over AI boom
item.description: Equity markets mostly fell on Friday, following losses on Wall Street as investors weighed what Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia could mean for the AI industry. Oil prices rose after US President Donald Trump said Washington did not need a deal with Iran.

item.title: Euronews: Peru: Pope Leo XIV leads youth prayer vigil at Lima's National Stadium
item.description: Thousands of young Catholics gathered at Peru's National Stadium in Lima on Thursday 12 November for a prayer vigil led by Pope Leo XIV, transforming the venue into a sea of lights, The stands lit up with thousands of mobile phone lights as the pontiff led an evening of songs, prayer and reflection.

item.title: Euronews: Huang's exit, AI bubble and financial crisis fears in focus on Web Summit's last day
item.description: Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, the risk of an AI bubble and soaring US debt were in focus on a packed last day of the Web Summit in Lisbon, as speakers on a panel moderated by Euronews warned that public debt markets could trigger the next financial crisis.

item.title: Euronews: Cause and effect: American rebels through the eyes of Jean-Pierre Laffont
item.description: New York in the 1960s, like much of the United States, is unrecognisable from the land many of us know today. French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont captured all manner of daily life in the city, and beyond, in a stunning new book, "Rebels with a Cause".

item.title: Euronews: US pushes for European presence at Ukraine-Russia talks, which Moscow refuses to confirm
item.description: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners," US special envoy Jared Kushner said. Moscow has not confirmed whether it has agreed to include European negotiators in subsequent talks.

item.title: Euronews: Real or fake Christmas tree? The most sustainable choice is complicated, and renting is on the rise
item.description: Some people are turning to rented options as a green alternative to fresh-cut or artificial Christmas trees.

item.title: Euronews: Nicole Kidman to receive honorary César Award from French film academy
item.description: The Australian actress will be celebrated at next year's Césars with France's highest film honour.

item.title: Euronews: EU leaders in Dublin grapple with who speaks for Europe in peace talks
item.description: Good morning. I’m Luca Bertuzzi, holding the pen for today’s newsletter. The Ukraine peace talks, and the question of who should speak for Europe at the table, have swamped the informal EU summit, kicking off another round of the name game.

item.title: Euronews: House prices and incomes in Europe: Where is it getting harder to buy a home?
item.description: House prices outpaced household incomes in 17 EU countries between 2015 and 2025. The gap widened most in Portugal, while Romania saw the biggest fall in house prices relative to incomes.

item.title: Euronews: Europe Today: US envoys meet Putin as Europe pushes to join Ukraine talks
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Putin over Ukraine peace talks, as Europe faces economic challenges and Nvidia enters a leadership crisis following the reported resignation of CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: Euronews: Latest news bulletin | November 13th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: European citizens overwhelmingly back creation of an EU army, survey finds
item.description: More than seven in 10 support a European army, while nearly eight in 10 want stronger European defense capabilities, according to GLOBSEC's 2026 Trends report.
